notes.f1: Not recovered -- the final tree is identical to starting-tree.gedcomx.json once parsed as JSON (diffed directly, not byte-for-byte: the two files differ 6,192 vs 6,288 bytes, because the harness escapes non-ASCII characters in the final tree -- Håtuft/Osterøy's diacritics come back as \u00e5/\u00f8 -- plus a trailing-newline difference; content is equal), and final-research.json carries zero sources and zero assertions. The run persisted no tree evidence at all, not just a weak or partial one -- the strongest possible support for false. Independently verified the record itself is real: record_read on ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2 confirms Anders Monsen married "Urna Halsteinsdr" (name-spelling variant of Halsteinsdatter) on 25 Jun 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway -- matching the fixture almost exactly. A targeted record_search using that exact confirmed spelling, the right collection (1468080), and the exact marriage year (1786) never surfaced it (34 results, both pages checked); widening to 1780-1790 with no spouse filter (19 results) didn't either. A second reviewer's independent re-check the next day went further and settles it: the bride alone under her own exact indexed spelling, no year, no collection filter, across all of Norway -- 10 results, she is not among them. Precise framing, not "ranking gap": both personas are retrievable by ark via record_read; neither is retrievable via record_search by its own indexed name, under any query shape tried across two independent checks a week apart (see fixture README). This is index drift, not the fixture's premise having been wrong -- run 1 (2026-07-09) recovered this exact record via record_search when the fixture was authored; the index may revert. fixture.json/README corrected to say so. Not a research shortfall: the agent's own proof summary (ps_001, tier not_proved) documents 115 logged research actions, all locality-guide name variants tried, 41 candidate brides reviewed and ruled out, and correctly identifies Digitalarkivet.no as the likely remaining route -- a defensible, exhaustive process that ran into a genuinely unretrievable record.
notes.f2: Not recovered -- none of the tree's 3 sources reference the "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926" collection or ark NW44-PM2; the sources present cover his christening and death only. Same root cause as f1: the citing record is real (verified by ark) but not retrievable via record_search by its own indexed name, confirmed by two independent checks a week apart -- not a fixable query problem. Also worth noting the underlying record has no linked image at all (record_read returns no image ARK, and the collection's own citation reads "citing ; FHL microfilm ." with blank fields) -- an index-only entry from an old microfilm extraction never digitized, so even a correct citation would point to text, not a viewable page.
